input: n is an integer with 0 <= n <= 65535. Zero requests an empty matrix. String inputs, when present, are ordinary str values, not subclasses. Integer values are plain int, excluding bool; lists are ordinary lists, not subclasses. There is no concurrent mutation or monkey-patching of standard built-ins. Preconditions are not checked at runtime. Allocation and runtime resource limits still require qualification; this declared domain is not a capacity or completion guarantee.
return: A fresh n-by-n matrix containing each integer from 1 through n*n exactly once in clockwise spiral order, beginning at the top-left cell and moving right first. n = 0 returns a fresh empty outer list.
mutation_aliasing: There is no mutable input. The outer matrix and every row are newly allocated; no two rows alias. All assigned values are immutable integers. Mutating a returned row cannot change another row or a later call. The Solution instance retains no state.
numeric: The maximum assigned value is 65535^2 = 4294836225, and the final incremented value is at most 4294836226. Dimensions, indices, boundary sentinels, products and counters remain exact safe integers in both languages. Python arbitrary-size integers do not broaden the paired dimension range.
complexity: O(n*n + 1) time including zero-filled row allocation and O(1) auxiliary space excluding O(n*n + n + 1) output storage. Each cell is initialized and then assigned once. Separate per-row allocations are charged. Four shrinking boundaries and guards prevent duplicate assignments on the central row/column; no recursion is used.
source_accounting: The complete standalone source is 951 UTF-8 bytes, including the Solution class, method signature, every loop, condition, allocation, standard built-in call, annotation/comment where present, whitespace and terminal newline. There are no custom helper definitions, imports, generated implementations or hidden source expansion.
